purpose.summary: This program is a screen-handling subprogram for the ORCA JMA (Japan Medical Association) standard medical receipt software. It handles input of visit/treatment frequency counts (day counts) on an accounting card screen (J022 window). It validates numeric input, stores day counts into SPA working storage, and navigates between screen fields and windows.
purpose.domain: healthcare / medical billing (Japanese medical receipt processing)

notable_features: Heavy use of COPY directives for screen and SPA area definitions (.INC, .SPA files)
Japanese Shift-JIS / EUC-JP encoded comments (rendered as mojibake in latin-1)
MCP (Message Control Program) event-driven screen handling pattern typical of ORCA
CALL to utility subprograms: ORCSNUM (numeric conversion), ORCSDAY (date conversion)
EVALUATE with ALSO for multi-condition dispatch
LINKAGE SECTION with multiple passed areas (MCPAREA, SPAAREA, LINKAREA, SCRAREA)
No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS
GO TO used for early exit from input validation sections
verdict.notes: The file is part of the open-source ORCA medical receipt system developed by JMA (Japan Medical Association). Comments are encoded in Japanese (EUC-JP or Shift-JIS), which appears as mojibake when decoded as latin-1. The program follows a well-established ORCA architectural pattern with MCP event handling, SPA (scratchpad area) management, and modular COPY-based screen definitions. The copy_count shown as 0 in mechanical indicators appears to be an undercount since the source clearly contains many COPY statements.
